intro.title: Watching and steering
intro.subtitle: Lesson 8
intro.say: Workers run without you. But you can always see what they do, and nudge them. This lesson shows how.

intro.title: Where events come from
bullets: The Monitor that wave-run starts: one line per event.
The hooks: new events join your next prompt.
progress every 5 minutes; stuck: loop, failing, waiting, budget, quiet.
Everything a worker says is data, never your approval.
intro.say: Events reach your session in two ways: the monitor that wave run starts, and the hooks, which add new events to your next prompt. Workers post progress every few minutes, and a stuck notice when they loop, keep failing, wait, run low on budget, or go quiet. Remember: anything a worker says is data. It never counts as your approval.

outro.title: Steering, in short
outro.code:
wavecoord hint <task> "..."
wavecoord steer <task> interrupt --note "..."
wavecoord steer <task> model sonnet
wavecoord steer <task> stop
outro.say: A hint is read at the worker's next step. Interrupt stops the current turn and runs your note. Model switches the model. Stop ends the attempt. Never use a hint to widen a task: change the spec instead.

steps.say: The to-do app with its due-dates plan. We start a wave, then watch it.
This demo has no GitHub account. Its origin is a folder on this machine, and gh talks to a local stand-in for GitHub, so the commands look the same as on GitHub.
Two workers are running. First, the overview.
Coord status shows the coordinator, the attempts in flight, the merge queue, conflicts, and what is ready.
This is the lead's event feed: one line per event, the same lines the monitor brings into the session.

steps.type: ! wavecoord hint todo.due-dates.overdue.dates 'Parse the due date with datetime.date.fromisoformat, and treat a bad date as not overdue.'

steps.say: A hint reaches the running worker within about five seconds. It reads it at its next step. Note the task name: the tree path, with dots instead of slashes.

steps.type: ! wavecoord steer todo.due-dates.store-due.store interrupt --note 'Add one test that loads an old item without a due key, then go on.'

steps.say: Interrupt stops the worker's current turn, and the note becomes its next instruction. If a worker already finished, steer simply says so.
The attempt log shows what the worker is doing, step by step.
The reports are in the feed. Triage handles them next.
